author: GamingBolt
description:
Resident Evil Requiem is an important entry in the franchise, and when all is said and done, it stands tall to the herculean task it undertakes. Releasing alongside the series’ 30th anniversary, it serves as a worthy follow-up to the overarching Resident Evil story, which had been dormant for some time now, while also being both, a meaningful step forward and a great introduction point for newcomers. 

It also successfully combines the best of Resident Evil’s horror and action peaks, delivering potent scares and pulse-pounding action with great aplomb, even with late-game stumbles. We’ll see with time where it ranks among the series’ best outings, but for now, I can confidently say that Resident Evil Requiem is yet another impressive high for the genre.
title: Resident Evil Requiem Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
An open world as vast as Crimson Desert's Pywel was always bound to attract comparisons to the Wild West from Red Dead Redemption. We say that's a good thing, as we got to think long and hard about why the two games were feeling increasingly similar to us. 

Did fantasy and gritty history have enough in common to even warrant that comparison? Perhaps not, but the design philosophies that underscore each experience are quite tangible, and are definitely worth examining for similarities. That's exactly what we've set out to do in this one. Join us for an interesting look at the things that make Pywel and the Wild West feel so similar even as they are different, and how there might finally be an open world that feels as good as the best there is.
title: Crimson Desert's World Almost Feels Like Red Dead Redemption 2 All Over Again
